subject: Uptime ledger discrepancy — third-party peering event counted against SLA
messages:
From: Helen Grant <ops@mediflow.com>
To: priya_natarajan@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@mediflow.com
Date: 2027-06-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Uptime credit request — June 1 peering flap

Hi Priya,

We ran our monthly availability reconciliation and Redwood is showing a 27-minute downtime on 2027-05-30 that you attributed to our account. Our SLO requires 99.95% availability; that 27-minute window pushed us under the threshold for May. From our side the issue looks like a TransitOne peering flap — they dropped routes, we had high latency and partial request failures for a region.

Can you confirm why the event was counted against our uptime rather than excluded as a third-party transit outage? We also need to understand the exact calculation (start/end timestamps, path-level vs global) since our finance team is asking about potential credits and this is blocking a renewal conversation.

I attached our latency graphs and a pcap summary. Please escalate — this is high priority for Mediflow.

Thanks,
Helen Grant
Head of IT, Mediflow Health
ops@mediflow.com

Attachments: mediflow_latency_graphs.png
From: priya_natarajan@redwood.com <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-01T09:38:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Uptime credit request — June 1 peering flap

Folks — forwarding Mediflow's note. They claim TransitOne peering caused a 27m window and want exclusion / credit clarification. Customer is escalated to procurement too.

Ask list:
- Laura: can you confirm whether our edge telemetry attributes this to an upstream peer (TransitOne) or internal routing? Please include the exact start/end timestamps you used for SLA.
- Marissa: hold customer-facing comms; I want a short internal alignment before we reply.
- Ben: we may need to calculate a credit estimate and check contract language on third-party exclusions.

I've attached the customer's graphs and asked them for the TransitOne contact.

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference

Attachments: mediflow_latency_graphs.png
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: priya_natarajan@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-01T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Uptime credit request — June 1 peering flap

Priya / team —

I pulled the edge telemetry and routing events. Short summary:
- We see a BGP route withdrawal affecting the us-west-2 POP that started at 2027-05-30T03:14:12Z and resolved at 2027-05-30T03:41:09Z (UTC). That aligns with ~26m57s of reduced successful requests for the US-WEST region.
- The root cause trace indicates TransitOne announced a withdrawal on their side; our peers show session resets at the same timestamps.
- However, our SLA calculation logic currently marks a customer-affecting event when 5%+ of global egress fails for at least 5 continuous minutes. For Mediflow, the aggregation used global traffic because they route across multiple POPs; the per-account path-level attribution was not applied because the request distribution in that window fell below our path-level threshold.

Net: the incident appears to be an upstream peer flap, but our current uptime ledger treats it as Redwood network-affecting because the global aggregation crossed our customer-impact threshold. This is a borderline case between path-level exclusion and global aggregation.

I've attached the raw BGP dump (transitone_bgp_dump.txt) and a short SLA calc workbook (sla_calc_sheet.xlsx) that shows how the 27m was computed. If legal/COGS says third-party exclusion should apply, we can mark this as excluded retroactively, but we need a documented rule tweak: prefer path-level attribution when >70% of a customer's traffic is unaffected.

Laura Bennett
Sr. Network Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: transitone_bgp_dump.txt, sla_calc_sheet.xlsx
From: ben_carter@redwood.com <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: priya_natarajan@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-02T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Uptime credit request — June 1 peering flap

Team —

Thanks Laura for the analysis. A few commercial notes:
- Mediflow is mid-enterprise, onboarding volume has been rising, and renewal is scheduled for July. This credit (if granted) will be material to the renewal negotiation.
- Contract excerpt (SLA §4.1): "Credits exclude outages caused by third-party telecommunications providers unless such provider is under Redwood's contractual control." There's ambiguity for peering.

Proposal for an initial customer-facing reply (keeping internal options open):
1) Acknowledge the disruption and share the timeline (start/end) from our telemetry.
2) Explain that telemetry shows an upstream peer route withdrawal; outline why our ledger currently included it (global aggregation threshold).
3) Offer a one-time proration credit equal to 7 days of service (or X% of monthly usage), subject to us completing a formal attribution review within 7 business days.

If legal wants strict adherence to exclusion only when the third party provides formal incident confirmation, we may need TransitOne's incident ticket to grant an automatic exclusion. Marissa — can you coordinate a customer-safe reply? Priya — I'll stand up the credit calc once we agree.

Ben Carter
Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
From: priya_natarajan@redwood.com <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: ops@mediflow.com, procurement@mediflow.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-04T17:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Uptime ledger discrepancy — third-party peering event counted against SLA

Hi Helen / Mark —

Thanks for flagging this and for the graphs you sent. Short summary from our side:
- We observed a route withdrawal affecting the US-WEST POP starting 2027-05-30T03:14:12Z and resolving 2027-05-30T03:41:09Z (UTC). Our telemetry shows reduced success rates in that interval.
- Initial attribution indicates the event was caused by an upstream peer (TransitOne). However, our current SLA ledger aggregated globally and the impact crossed our internal customer-impact threshold, so the downtime was counted in May's tally.

To keep things moving while we complete a formal attribution:
- We're offering a one-time prorated credit equal to 7 days of service (applied to your next invoice) while we pursue a full attribution review with TransitOne. If TransitOne confirms responsibility, we'll convert this to a formal third-party exclusion and remove the downtime from your May availability tally.
- Next steps: Mediflow — can you share any TransitOne incident ticket you received? TransitOne — can you confirm whether a session withdrawal occurred for our peering on 2027-05-30 and share your incident ID?

We want to be transparent and move quickly here so it doesn't impact your renewal. I'll follow up with a short postmortem and a proposal for a ledger rule change (path-level preference when >70% of traffic unaffected).

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
priya_natarajan@redwood.com
